stories.headline: Google DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2, predicting DNA variant effects in specific cell types

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on November 11, 2026, a model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variants affect specific human cell types.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are announcing AlphaGenome 2, our next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types

key_facts.fact: The model was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues and identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression as DeepMind's previous model.
key_facts.excerpt: AlphaGenome 2 identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression in cells, compared to our previous state-of-the-art model. Trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues

key_facts.fact: On the TenK10K dataset of 28 immune cell types, AlphaGenome 2 identified 30% of causal variants versus 16% for the original AlphaGenome, and 43% of directional gene effects versus 23%.
key_facts.excerpt: AlphaGenome 2 reliably identified nearly twice as many causal variants (30% vs. 16%) and directional gene effects (43% vs. 23%) as the original AlphaGenome fine-tuned on single-cell data

key_facts.fact: AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model that adapts to new single-cell experiments from just a few dozen cells without retraining, and adds DNA methylation predictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Scientists can upload a single-cell RNA-seq snapshot of gene activity from just a few dozen cells ... The model predicts the same core experimental readouts ... but also DNA methylation, a widely requested readout.

key_facts.fact: The model covers 637 human and 311 mouse cell types it was trained on, according to Nature.
key_facts.excerpt: The model also isn't limited to making predictions in the 637 types of human and 311 mouse cells it was trained with.

key_facts.fact: AlphaGenome 2 is available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API, with a private preview for commercial research.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says it is making AlphaGenome 2 available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API from today, with a limited 'private preview' for commercial research.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a model that scores choices instead of generating text

key_facts.fact: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, powered by a new model, Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

key_facts.fact: The model evaluates up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice and rubric questions against one multimodal input of up to 256K tokens in a single forward pass, with 150-250 ms end-to-end latency.
key_facts.excerpt: You can pass one multimodal input across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) along with up to 1,000 independent questions ... returning probabilities and confidence scores in 150-250 ms end-to-end latency

key_facts.fact: Pricing is $0.10 per 1M input tokens with zero output tokens billed.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens

key_facts.fact: Google targets the small branching calls inside agents: routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading.
key_facts.excerpt: For developers, this targets the small branching calls inside agents: routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading.

key_facts.fact: The launch puts Google in a market with TypeSafe's Jev, OpenAI's Decisions API running on GPT-6 Luna, and Amazon's Strands Decider.
key_facts.excerpt: That puts Google into a market where TypeSafe's Jev already handles inexpensive classification, OpenAI's Decisions API runs on GPT-6 Luna, and Amazon's Strands Decider gives developers the option to run the model on their own infrastructure.

stories.headline: AWS releases AWS Emulator, a local cloud stand-in written and maintained entirely by AI agents

key_facts.fact: AWS released AWS Emulator on November 11, 2026, a local emulator of AWS services that developers and coding agents can run on their own machines with no AWS account and no service fee.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting today, you can use AWS Emulator to build and test AWS applications on your computer or in your continuous integration (CI) environment ... with no deployments or AWS account required.

key_facts.fact: AWS says thousands of autonomous AI agents wrote every line of code and the team has not written or reviewed any of it.
key_facts.excerpt: The emulator was written entirely by autonomous agents. Our team hasn't written or reviewed any of the code.

key_facts.fact: Three teams of agents run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: one writes fidelity tests checked against real AWS, one files issues for failures, and one fixes them, one agent per issue; hundreds of agents fix thousands of issues a day.
key_facts.excerpt: The agents run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in three teams ... Goldberg wrote that hundreds of agents now fix thousands of issues a day.

key_facts.fact: The emulator is built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services.
key_facts.excerpt: It's built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services.

key_facts.fact: The source code is published on GitHub under a CC0 public-domain dedication; AWS warns it does not evaluate IAM policies and should not be used for security testing.
key_facts.excerpt: Don't use the emulator to test whether your application is secure. It doesn't evaluate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies and resource-based policies the way AWS does

stories.headline: United Airlines bans third-party AI agents from booking flights; CEO wants no 'another middleman'

key_facts.fact: United Airlines said on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, it would restrict unauthorized third-party AI agents from its digital platforms, directly and via travel agencies and aggregators, citing data security.
key_facts.excerpt: United Airlines said on Wednesday it would restrict AI bots' access to its digital platforms, citing data security ... both directly through its digital platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators

key_facts.fact: United's November 11 contract-of-carriage revision bans the use of AI agents to make, modify or service a ticket, even under human supervision, and lets United cancel such reservations.
key_facts.excerpt: Rule 6.J.6 bans: The use of AI Agents to make, modify or service a Ticket ... Human supervision or approval doesn't circumvent that. And its Rule 5.H gives United the right to cancel reservations

key_facts.fact: CEO Scott Kirby said: 'To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman,' United CEO Scott Kirby said at an event on Tuesday, according to the Journal.

key_facts.fact: Agents can still display United flights and prices but cannot complete the transaction; United cites possible FAA and DOT rule violations, such as automated check-in skipping the hazardous-materials acknowledgment.
key_facts.excerpt: These automated AI actions have the potential to violate FAA and DOT regulations - as an example, flight check-in requires human acknowledgment that bags do not contain banned substances like explosives.

key_facts.fact: Agent bookings made before November 11, 2026 will not be canceled.
key_facts.excerpt: agent bookings made prior to November 11, 2026 will not be canceled

key_facts.fact: Amazon has blocked Meta's AI agent Muse while Walmart partnered with it, and Expedia and Booking work with OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon has blocked Meta's AI agent Muse, while Walmart has partnered with it. Meanwhile, online travel firms such as Expedia and Booking are working with ChatGPT-parent OpenAI.

stories.headline: Nvidia board meets on ousting Jensen Huang after second affair report; CFO Kress eyed as interim CEO

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's board met on Wednesday, Nov 11, to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, after the Wall Street Journal reported the board was preparing to force him out; no decision had been announced by Thursday morning.
key_facts.excerpt: The board met Wednesday to discuss Mr. Huang but has made no announcement about any decision regarding Nvidia's longtime leader.

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang had a separate extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports to him; this followed his admission of an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive US intelligence suspects of spying for China.
key_facts.excerpt: Huang's position became more tenuous late on Wednesday after it was reported by the New York Times that Huang had a separate extramarital affair with a company employee named Kimberly Powell.

key_facts.fact: Some board members favor naming CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, and the board has debated adding a chief operating officer alongside an interim chief; Nvidia briefed the White House on its planned meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's board has debated whether, as part of its potential replacement of Huang, to introduce a chief operating officer to serve alongside the interim chief executive, some of the people said.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has tapped an outside search firm to find a successor; Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is among those being considered, per Semafor citing Bloomberg and a source.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has tapped an outside search firm to find the company's next CEO, Bloomberg reported. One person being considered for the top job is Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji

key_facts.fact: Under Nvidia's bylaws Huang can be removed with or without cause by a majority of its 11 directors; Huang, 63, owns about 3.6% of the stock and has no obvious successor.
key_facts.excerpt: Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of directors. Nvidia has 11 directors and considers all but Huang independent.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after-hours trading after the WSJ report, hitting a 52-week low.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading, hitting a 52-week low.

key_facts.fact: Rivals gained: AMD closed up 7.3% and rose 4%+ pre-market, while Broadcom gained 4% and then 2.4% pre-market as Nvidia's board weighed ousting Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD's shares rose 4%+ pre-market, after closing up 7.3%, and Broadcom gained 2.4% pre-market, following a 4% gain, as Nvidia's board weighs ousting Jensen Huang

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is due to report quarterly results on Nov 17; Polymarket put the odds of Huang resigning or being removed by year-end at 88%.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is due to report its quarterly results on November 17 ... Polymarket put the probability of Huang resigning or being removed by the end of the year at 88%.

stories.headline: Commerce readies rule on remote chip access as Chinese AI firms rush to rent Nvidia capacity abroad

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department is finalizing a long-awaited rule to stop Chinese AI firms from remotely accessing advanced AI chips through data centers in other countries, The Information reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: the US Commerce Department is finalizing a semiconductor control update that would prevent remote access and chip smuggling into China via data centers

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered capacity at data centers outside China; a major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally locking in overseas capacity and smaller labs are approaching Southeast Asian compute-rental providers, Reuters reported on Nov 12 citing three people.
key_facts.excerpt: A major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have contacted data-centre operators about reserving it, the people said.

key_facts.fact: The firms fear the Huang scandal will give momentum to the Remote Access Security Act, which the House passed 369-22 in January and which awaits Senate action.
key_facts.excerpt: The House of Representatives passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and it awaits Senate action.

key_facts.fact: Traders and intermediaries in China's grey market have started stockpiling restricted Nvidia chips in anticipation of tougher enforcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The prospect of tougher enforcement has also fuelled demand for restricted Nvidia AI chips in China's grey market, prompting traders and intermediaries to start stockpiling these processors

key_facts.fact: Alibaba shares fell as much as 7.1% in Hong Kong on Thursday, while Z.ai and MiniMax each lost 7% or more.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Alibaba, Z.ai and MiniMax fell in Hong Kong on Thursday. Alibaba shed up to 7.1% at its low point, and the other two each lost 7% or more.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed said on Thursday it had assisted inspectors from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security and hired a US law firm to catalog its GPUs, rejecting claims it illegally sent chips to China.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said Thursday that it had assisted inspectors from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security and engaged a U.S. law firm to catalog its graphics processing units.

key_facts.fact: A Baker McKenzie attorney told The Information that Commerce lacks statutory authority to regulate remote access under existing law, and Commerce is still consulting other agencies before finalizing the rule.
key_facts.excerpt: A Baker McKenzie attorney told The Information the department lacks that authority under existing statute ... Commerce is still consulting other agencies before the rule can be finalized

stories.headline: Axios: Lutnick stalled Trump-approved crackdown on Nvidia chip diversion to China three times

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has resisted restricting companies suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips to China, even though Trump approved action at least three times this year, in May, August and on Nov 5, Axios reported on Nov 11.
key_facts.excerpt: On at least three separate occasions — in May, August, and Nov. 5 — Trump approved taking action against suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China. But Lutnick and Commerce Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler resisted pressure

key_facts.fact: In a Situation Room meeting, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over why Megaspeed had not been added to the Entity List; Defense Secretary Hegseth, USTR Greer and Secretary of State Rubio sided with Bessent.
key_facts.excerpt: At a White House Situation Room meeting on Thursday after the midterm elections, Bessent pressed Lutnick on why Megaspeed had not been added to the Commerce Department's entity list, to which Lutnick responded he would "look into it."

key_facts.fact: Trump called Elon Musk before approving the crackdown; Musk backed the hawks while Lutnick warned it 'will start a trade war with China', then proposed developing 'options' after Trump said 'Let's get it done.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump called tech advisor Elon Musk and agreed to move forward. Musk supported Rubio, Bessent, Greer and Hegseth's case to impose the controls while Lutnick warned it "will start a trade war with China."

key_facts.fact: The Commerce Department denied that the Bessent-Lutnick confrontation took place.
key_facts.excerpt: "This is false. Secretary Bessent and Secretary Lutnick had no such conversation," spokesperson Kristen Eichamer said.

key_facts.fact: The US has posted no additions to its Entity List since October 2025, the longest gap in more than a decade.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. has not posted any additions to its Entity List since October 2025, the longest stretch between new postings in more than a decade.

key_facts.fact: Senators Chris Coons and Elizabeth Warren on Wednesday asked Lutnick, Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to preserve documents on Nvidia chip exports to China and on Huang and the suspected Chinese operative.
key_facts.excerpt: Sens. Chris Coons, D-Del., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., sent a letter to members of President Donald Trump's Cabinet on Wednesday asking them to preserve documents related to Nvidia's chip exports to China

stories.headline: CoreWeave plans at least $4B chip-backed investment-grade loan at about half its junk-bond yield

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave is preparing to raise at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan led by Morgan Stanley and MUFG that could launch as early as next week, Bloomberg reported on Nov 11.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction, led by Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc., would be syndicated in phases and could launch as early as next week, though terms remain subject to change.

key_facts.fact: Early pricing points to a 7%-7.5% yield, roughly half the yield on its existing high-yield debt; its 9.625% notes due 2032 traded at a 14.21% yield on Nov 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Preliminary discussions put the new loan's yield at 7% to 7.5%, roughly half the yield on CoreWeave's existing junk bonds ... CoreWeave's 9.625% notes due July 2032 traded at a 14.21% yield on 11 November.

key_facts.fact: The junk-rated company is structuring the loan around its computing hardware and customer contracts, mirroring an $8.5 billion investment-grade facility backed by Meta contracts in March.

stories.headline: Zelensky says Starshield speed cap is back, letting Russian jet drones slip past interceptors

key_facts.fact: On November 12, 2026, Zelensky said Ukrainian units had recorded significant disruptions to Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink, for several days along the entire front line and in occupied territories.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's military is once again experiencing significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications system, the militarized version of Starlink, for several days, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Nov. 12.

key_facts.fact: The restrictions cut connectivity for equipment moving faster than 161 km/h (100 mph), and Zelensky said they were 'not random errors but systematic speed restrictions'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Specifically, systematic speed restrictions are being imposed on Starshield, limiting it to 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour)," Zelenskyy wrote on X. He said Ukraine's military had investigated the disruptions and concluded they were not random technical errors but systematic restrictions.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said some Russian strikes had already got through because interceptors could not reach the speed needed to catch Russian jet-powered drones; the Geran-4 typically flies at 300-400 km/h.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said the renewed cap is primarily disrupting efforts to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The Geran-4, for example, typically flies at 300–400 kilometers per hour (185–250 miles per hour), according to Ukraine's Defense Intelligence.

key_facts.fact: The cap returned less than three weeks after Ukraine's Defense Ministry said on October 24 that connectivity had been restored at speeds above 400 km/h, following a first cap recorded on October 13-14.
key_facts.excerpt: On 24 October, Ukraine's Defence Ministry confirmed that connectivity had been restored, with stable connections at speeds exceeding 400 kilometres per hour. The restrictions were first recorded overnight on 13–14 October

key_facts.fact: Neither Washington nor SpaceX has accepted responsibility; Musk has said Starshield systems are 'owned and controlled by the US government', and Kyiv says it is trying to establish the circumstances with the US.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said decisions over Starshield speed restrictions were made by the US military and ultimately the US president, writing on X that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government." Neither Washington nor SpaceX have publicly accepted responsibility

key_facts.fact: Senior Ukrainian officials told the FT they believe the restrictions were imposed to pressure Kyiv during the latest peace talks with Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: Senior Ukrainian officials told @FT they believed the Starshield speed restrictions were imposed in an effort to pressure Kyiv during the latest peace talks with Russia.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's agreement with Washington for Starshield access expires in mid-2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The renewed disruptions come as Kyiv seeks to extend its agreement with Washington for access to Starshield, which is set to expire in mid-2027.

stories.headline: Ukraine-born drone maker Uforce raises $700M at $6B, with UK wealth fund's largest defense bet

key_facts.fact: Uforce, founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, announced on November 12, 2026 a $700 million Series A at a $6 billion valuation, co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK National Wealth Fund.
key_facts.excerpt: UFORCE, a defence-technology company founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, with major hubs in Kyiv and Washington, DC, today announced a $700 million Series A financing round at a valuation of $6 billion.

key_facts.fact: The National Wealth Fund put in $150 million, its largest defense investment, making Uforce the UK's most valuable defense startup; Valor is run by Musk ally Antonio Gracias.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK National Wealth Fund made its largest defense investment ... Valor Equity Partners, an investment firm run by Elon Musk ally Antonio Gracias ... The financing, including $150 million from the NWF, gives London-based Uforce a valuation of $6 billion, making it the UK's most valuable defense startup.

key_facts.fact: The valuation is about six times the roughly $1 billion at which Uforce raised $50 million in March; CEO Oleg Rogynskyy said bookings more than doubled over the past year from a base of several hundred million dollars.
key_facts.excerpt: UFORCE ... raised $50 million at a valuation of around $1 billion in March. ... UFORCE CEO Oleg Rogynskyy told CNBC that the company's bookings have more than doubled over the past year, from a base of several hundred million dollars

key_facts.fact: The U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund also participated, and former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe Gen. Christopher Cavoli joins the board.
key_facts.excerpt: with participation from the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. ... General (Ret.) Christopher G. Cavoli, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe and Partner at Valor Equity Partners, joins the UFORCE board.

key_facts.fact: Uforce says its Nemesis drones have flown more than 300,000 combat flights and its Magura naval drones helped destroy more than a dozen Russian warships in the Black Sea.
key_facts.excerpt: UFORCE says its NEMESIS drones have completed more than 300,000 combat flights, while its MAGURA naval vessels have contributed to the destruction of more than a dozen Russian warships in the Black Sea.

key_facts.fact: The money will scale manufacturing in Ukraine and allied countries across the US, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: The company plans to use the new funding to scale manufacturing in Ukraine and in allied countries, including the U.S., Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.

stories.headline: Yen nears 160 per dollar as Fed hike bets lift the dollar; Tokyo warns of renewed intervention

key_facts.fact: The dollar rose to 159.94 yen early on November 12, its strongest in more than two months, driven by bets on Fed rate hikes after hot US inflation data.
key_facts.excerpt: The dollar rose to 159.94 against the Japanese yen early on Thursday, hitting its strongest in more than two months, buoyed by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates after hot US inflation data

key_facts.fact: Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura said recent moves were too fast and that it is 'too early to forget' the summer intervention, his first FX remarks since late September.
key_facts.excerpt: In his first remarks on foreign exchange since late September, Mimura said he believed recent currency moves have been excessively rapid. "It's still too early to forget what happened this summer,"

key_facts.fact: Japan spent a record 15.4 trillion yen on interventions over three days between July 30 and August 3, including one run jointly with the US, when the yen neared 164 per dollar.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan last conducted interventions on three days between July 30 and August 3, spending a record total of 15.4 trillion yen over the month, as the Japanese currency reached its weakest levels in 40 years near 164 per dollar.

key_facts.fact: Japan's yen-based import price index jumped 24.8% year on year in October.
key_facts.excerpt: The yen-based import price index jumped 24.8% in October from a year earlier, data showed on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The US dollar index reached 103.08, its highest since April 2025; markets fully price a December Fed hike, with a small chance of 50 basis points.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Dollar Index (DXY) ... trades near 102.88 after reaching 103.08, its highest level since April 2025. Traders now fully price in a December Fed rate hike, with a 25-basis-point (bps) move the most likely outcome and a small chance of a larger 50 bps increase.

key_facts.fact: On November 11, the euro hit a 19-month low, European stocks closed at a record high and gold fell back below $4,000 an ounce.
key_facts.excerpt: FX: Dollar hits 19-month high, euro 19-month low. Dollar/yen nears 160.00. ... Europe +0.7% to new closing high ... Gold -1% back below $4,000/oz.

key_facts.fact: Mizuho analysts said Tokyo could intervene unilaterally if the dollar breaks above 160 and a weaker yen fuels inflation.
key_facts.excerpt: "If the dollar breaks above 160 and the weaker yen fuels inflation, increasing the risk of a decline in support for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government, Tokyo could carry out unilateral intervention," they added.

stories.headline: NYSE owner ICE and OKX set Nov. 23 launch of tokenized stock venue after dozens of issuers object

key_facts.fact: On November 11, 2026, OKXICE, the 50-50 joint venture of NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, said its Tokenized Securities Venue opens at 9am ET on November 23.
key_facts.excerpt: OKXICE, the crypto exchange OKX's joint venture with NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), said on Nov. 11 that its Tokenized Securities Venue (TSV) will open for trading at 9 a.m. ET on Nov. 23.

key_facts.fact: More than 70 assets are confirmed, including Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood and Strategy (with its preferred stock), plus 59 Direxion ETFs, though not all will trade on day one.
key_facts.excerpt: more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion.

key_facts.fact: The venture's November 5 notice listed 67 issuers that objected to having their shares tokenized, including Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta and Goldman Sachs.
key_facts.excerpt: The venture's own public notice, dated Nov. 5 and published as the exemption requires, lists 67 issuers that had sent it a notice of objection by that date, among them Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta and Goldman Sachs.

key_facts.fact: The venue operates under the SEC's five-year 'innovation exemption' issued September 17, which lets it trade tokenized stocks without registering as an exchange; it is the second venue to launch under it.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, OKX and ICE announced it would launch its TSV on Nov. 23 as part of the SEC's five-year innovation exemption that debuted in September to bring capital markets in the U.S. on-chain and not have to register as more traditional exchanges.

key_facts.fact: Trading runs 24/7 through Uniswap v4 pools on OKX's X Layer network, with Securitize tokenizing shares one-for-one and holders keeping dividends and voting rights in self-custodied wallets.
key_facts.excerpt: Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 and deployed on X Layer ... Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by a U.S. share ... holders keep the usual shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions

key_facts.fact: Former New York governor Andrew Cuomo co-chairs OKXICE; ICE and OKX formed the venture in June after ICE invested in OKX at a $25 billion valuation in March.
key_facts.excerpt: said Andrew Cuomo, the former New York governor who co-chairs OKXICE with Trabue Bland ... ICE and OKX formed the joint venture in June, after ICE invested in OKX at a $25 billion valuation in March.

stories.headline: ESA's Euclid releases first major data batch: 900M+ galaxies toward a 3D map of the dark universe

key_facts.fact: On November 12, 2026, ESA released DR1-Foundation, the Euclid space telescope's first major data release, capturing light from more than a billion objects over a sky area as big as 9,500 full Moons.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has released its first major batch of data. With this release, which captures the light of more than a billion objects and covers an area of sky as big as 9500 full Moons

key_facts.fact: The release includes over 900 million galaxies, about 15,000 strong gravitational lensing candidates, over 60 million quasar candidates and spectra from more than 160 million sources.
key_facts.excerpt: Over 900 million galaxies; Around 15 000 strong gravitational lensing candidates; Over 60 million quasar candidates ... The spectra from more than 160 million sources

key_facts.fact: DR1-Foundation covers about 13 months of observations, 1,900 square degrees and 1.7 million GB of data, roughly 14% of the area Euclid will eventually survey.
key_facts.excerpt: The new data release, named DR1-Foundation and consisting of 1.7 million GB of data, comprises around 13 months of observations ... This dataset still only covers about 14% of the total sky area Euclid will survey

key_facts.fact: Euclid is a €1.4 billion mission whose goal is to probe dark energy and dark matter, thought to make up about 70% and 25% of the universe.
key_facts.excerpt: The goal is to shed light on two of the biggest mysteries in the universe: the nature of dark energy and dark matter. These are thought to make up about 70% and 25% of the universe respectively.

key_facts.fact: ESA science director Carole Mundell called it 'the largest space-based survey of its kind'; the full Data Release 1, adding weak lensing and galaxy-cluster data, is due in mid-2027.
key_facts.excerpt: "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy" ... with the first full data release set for mid-2027.
